U0001.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus
U0001.description: A general fault on the high-speed CAN bus has been detected. This bus typically connects powertrain modules (ECM, TCM, ABS) at 500 kbit/s and a fault disables communication between them, often triggering multiple secondary DTCs in other modules.

causes.label: CAN-High and CAN-Low shorted together
Open circuit in CAN bus wiring
Terminating resistor failed (not 60 ohms across bus)

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0002.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus Performance
U0002.description: The high-speed CAN bus is functional but performance is degraded — frame errors, bit errors or excessive bus load have been detected. Communication may be intermittent rather than completely lost, leading to sporadic warning lamps.

causes.label: Corrosion or poor contact in CAN connectors
Electromagnetic interference (aftermarket electronics)
One module sending malformed frames

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0003.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) Open
U0003.description: The CAN-High line of the high-speed bus is open. Without the differential pair, the controller cannot decode any traffic and reports loss of all participating modules at once. Often follows a wiring repair, accident damage, or a corroded connector pin.

causes.label: CAN-High wire broken or pin pushed back
Corroded module connector
Harness damage after repair or accident

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0004.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) Low
U0004.description: The CAN-High signal stays below its valid voltage window. Common cause is a short to ground on the CAN-H wire or a transceiver that pulls the line down. The bus stops working until the offending node is isolated.

causes.label: CAN-High shorted to ground
Internal transceiver failure on a node
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0005.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) High
U0005.description: The CAN-High line is held above its valid voltage range, usually because of a short to battery voltage. Bus communication collapses for every connected module.

causes.label: CAN-High shorted to battery voltage
Chafed harness against power wire
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0006.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) Open
U0006.description: The CAN-Low wire of the high-speed bus is open. The differential signal can no longer be evaluated correctly, so all bus participants report communication loss simultaneously.

causes.label: CAN-Low wire broken
Pin pushed back in connector
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0007.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) Low
U0007.description: The CAN-Low line is shorted to ground or held below its valid recessive level. The differential pair cannot transmit data and the bus is effectively dead.

causes.label: CAN-Low shorted to ground
Failed transceiver on one module
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0008.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) High
U0008.description: The CAN-Low signal is held above its valid range, typically because of a short to battery voltage on the CAN-L wire. Bus communication is lost for every node sharing this segment.

U0029.title: Vehicle Communication Bus A Performance
U0029.description: U0029 reports degraded communication although no hard wiring fault is identified: frames get lost, error counters rise or messages arrive late on vehicle communication bus A. SAE J2012 gives each vehicle bus a block of codes: the bus itself, performance, then open, low and high for the (+) and the (-) line and a short between them; which physical network carries which letter is set by the manufacturer. Modules on the affected bus may stop exchanging data, so lost-communication codes and warning lights in several systems usually appear together.

causes.label: Intermittent contact in a bus connector
Missing or faulty bus termination
A defective module disturbing the bus

symptoms: Several warning lights at once
Lost-communication codes stored in other modules
Functions of modules on this bus inoperative
Scan tool cannot reach some modules

U0073.title: Control Module Communication Bus "A" Off
U0073.description: A control module has detected that the communication bus is non-functional and has shut its bus interface off. Affects multiple modules at once because none can communicate; on most vehicles the dashboard lights up with several warning lamps simultaneously.

causes.label: CAN line shorted to supply or ground
Terminating resistor failed
One failing module pulling the bus down

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0074.title: Control Module Communication Bus "B" Off
U0074.description: A control module has shut its bus B interface off because the bus is non-functional. Bus B is typically a secondary CAN segment (often body or chassis) and a failure disables all modules connected to it.

causes.label: Bus B line shorted to supply or ground
One failing module pulling the bus down
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0075.title: Control Module Communication Bus C Off
U0075.description: U0075 means a control module has gone 'bus off' on communication bus C: its CAN controller counted so many transmit errors that, as the CAN protocol requires, it stopped sending. SAE numbers these codes by bus letter (U0073 bus A, U0074 bus B, U0075 bus C and so on up to U007F); the assignment of letters to networks is the manufacturer's. Until the controller recovers, the module cannot exchange data, so its own functions and those that depend on its messages drop out.

causes.label: Shorted or open bus wiring
Faulty bus termination
Defective transceiver in the reporting module

symptoms: Several warning lights at once
Lost-communication codes stored in other modules
Functions of modules on this bus inoperative
Scan tool cannot reach some modules

causes.label: Wire broken
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults
